section.title: Too many choices
section.intro:
When it comes to making a career, it's important to note that there are many different paths you can take. It's not just about getting enough points on the CAO. PLC courses offer an alternative path in, often without even taking any extra time. Transferring from another course is also an option, whilst there is always the option to study somewhere else in Europe, and in some places it's even cheaper than studying at home.

Finally, apprenticeships and trades give the option to learn and work at the same time, from accountancy and finance apprenticeships to plumbing and carpentry, there's something that matches any type of skillset.

items.body:
An apprenticeship is a job with training included. You are an employee from day one and you split your time between working and a classroom. By the end of it you have practical experience and a qualification

Apprenticeships stopped being only trades some time ago. There are apprenticeships in software, insurance, accountancy, engineering and logistics. Some even come with a degree.

blocks.heading: The hardest part is not the exams
blocks.text: It is finding an employer. There's no structured system the same way there is with the CAO. You have to get a company to say yes. Knowing somebody helps, which is the entire reason this website exists.

items.summary: Learn on the job, with a big salary by the time your friends have just finished college

myths.myth: You'll earn less in the end.
myths.reality: The power of earning money quickly... If you can get a mortgage sooner then you're already better off than those college grads paying 1k a month for a shoebox studio

items.title: Apprenticeships

items.body: A Post Leaving Certificate course is a full-time, practical course run by an Education and Training Board or a further education college. You apply directly. There is no points requirement.

blocks.heading: The backdoor
blocks.text: Upon completion, many PLCs have an arrangement to do an additional year at a university to earn a degree. For some courses it is a more reliable way into the same degree than competing on points. Ask the college which courses their students move into after completing their PLC

blocks.heading: The deadlines aren't as set
blocks.text: No central system means no set closing date. Plenty of colleges take applications deep into the summer, including after results come out. It gives you plenty of opportunity to consider your options

items.summary: A year or two, and you apply straight to the college.

items.title: PLC and further education

items.body:
Irish citizens, as EU students, get to pay the local rate anywhere in the union. In several countries that figure is small. Hundreds of degrees are taught entirely in English.

The Netherlands is the best known route. A large number of English language bachelor's degrees, a friendly application system, and student cities with a big international network. Germany and the Nordics teach in English too, at low or no tuition.

blocks.heading: Entry works differently
blocks.text: Many European universities don't run a points race. Some admit anyone who meets a minimum standard, some use a lottery, some choose for themselves. A course that is unreachable on points here may not be unreachable there.

blocks.heading: Sort out housing early
blocks.text: Not fees. Beds. Student accommodation in Dutch cities is genuinely scarce and has to be sorted early.

blocks.heading: Check what Irish support follows you
blocks.text: Some Irish student supports apply to study elsewhere in the EU and some do not, best to check with SUSi.

blocks.heading: What you get that isn't on the certificate
blocks.text: Living somewhere else at nineteen changes what you think is available to you. If you have not travelled much, that is the larger half of the value.

items.summary: English-taught degrees across the continent at EU fee rates. A fraction of what the same thing costs in the UK, and sometimes less than Dublin.
